# Pradaxa

Pradaxa is a direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) whose patient-facing information material is recommended for use in structured patient education about atrial fibrillation [^src1]. It is mentioned once in the corpus, in a list of manufacturer-produced pamphlets — alongside Xarelto, Eliquis, and Lixiana — plus regional pamphlets on anticoagulation (AK) treatment, which are named as materials suitable for informing patients [^src1].

The mention appears within a chapter documenting Indicator 8 (Structured patient education) of the AFDK programme (Atrieflimren i Danmark), run under the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram. That chapter lays out the evidence base for patient education as an integrated part of atrial fibrillation care, drawing on European ESC guidelines and Danish national recommendations, and describes the ABC Pathway model of integrated atrial fibrillation management (stroke prevention, better symptom control, and cardiovascular risk reduction), as well as the Danish health clusters participating in the AFDK programme. Pradaxa's information material is cited in this context as one of several resources clinicians can draw on when educating patients about anticoagulation therapy.

No further details — such as relationships to other entities, formal claims, or timeline events — are available for Pradaxa in this corpus.
